newsitem.title: UK: ABP still confident will escape windfall tax.
newsitem.headline: ABP still confident will escape windfall tax.

text.p: Associated British Ports Plc, the UK's largest port operator, reiterated on Wednesday its belief that it would escape the opposition Labour Party's windfall tax on utilities if the party won the next election.
ABP was tipped as a windfall tax target in a recent report by the Financial Times.

But Sir Keith Stuart, ABP chairman, said at a press conference on the annual results: "I am confident that there is no case for being included," pointing out that ABP had no price regulation or an industry regulator similar to those operating in utility industries like water or electricity.
"There is an Ofgas, Ofwat, Oftel and Offer (regulators for the gas, water, telecoms and electricity industries). But there is no Ofport," said the chairman of ABP.
He added that if Labour, which is expected to win the election due by May 22, did foist the tax on ABP "It would drive jobs and business to places like Rotterdam -- a subsidised port."
Also at the press briefing, the chairman said future tonnage growth was expected to remain in line with that of UK GDP, after growing by around three percent last year.
He repeated earlier comments by finance director Charles Orange that recent stg strength had no impact on profits.
Commenting on ABP's pitch to run Ipswich port, with the winner due to be announced soon, Stuart said there was considerable room for development.
"The port used to be a major player. But Ipswich is now a shadow of its former self. I am confident given the right approach, Ipswich can return to profitability and viability."
He said it had the potential to handle short sea container traffic, roll-on and roll-off and general cargo.
